articleTitle: Observations from the High-Speed Imaging of Dielectric Breakdown in Space-Charged Polymer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In this experiment, the dynamics of high-speed electrical tree growth in electron-charged bulk polymethyl methacrylate were studied using a gigahertz frame rate camera. In the first of two experimental runs, samples were charged using a 4.5 MeV electron Dynamitron accelerator and transported to Los Alamos National Laboratory for imaging. Dielectric breakdown was induced in each sample using an exploding bridge wire detonator and the formation of the subsequent electrical trees were imaged using a SIMX16 framing camera. Through this first imaging campaign and a subsequent campaign undertaken a year later, the propagation of the electrical tree was found to exhibit several distinct sequences: initiation, continued propagation, and cessation. It was found that the electron detrapping occurs simultaneously with the electrical tree damage propagation, with the electron detrapping occurring in a narrow band at the propagation front edge. Further, backlit images of the discharge revealed shock propagation off the already formed channels, proving that the damage trails that form the electrical tree are forming faster than the speed of sound in the material.

articleTitle: Electrical Insulation Lifetime of TiO2/Silicone Gel Nanocomposite in a Needle-plane Electrode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Silicone gel is used for an encapsulating material in power semiconductor modules. However, the voltage endurance of silicone gel is substantially reduced due to the generation of an electrical tree, which refers to a deterioration involving internal cavities that spread similar to trees. In this study, we investigated the electrical insulation lifetime of silicone gel caused by electrical treeing (treeing breakdown lifetime) and the extension of the lifetime due to the addition of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanofillers to the silicone gel. A needle-plane electrode molded by silicone gel nanocomposite or unfilled silicone gel was constructed for evaluating the breakdown caused by electrical treeing. The treeing breakdown lifetimes of silicone gel nanocomposite and unfilled silicone gel were measured when 7 kVrms or and 6 kVrms of AC voltage of 600 Hz was applied. The breakdown tests revealed that silicone gel nanocomposite has a longer lifetime than unfilled silicone gel when the 7 kVrms or and 6 kVrms is applied. These results indicate that the addition of the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanofillers to silicone gel can extend the treeing breakdown lifetime.

articleTitle: High Temperature Capacitor Films Based on Grafted Polypropylene with Varied Melt Indices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Polypropylene dielectric capacitors are critical energy storage devices in high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission systems. However, their energy density and charge-discharge efficiency rapidly decline at high temperatures, failing to meet the current high-temperature operational requirements. Graft modification is a method for developing high-temperature capacitor films with high energy density, thermal stability, and excellent electrical properties. The changes in the melt index caused by grafting are key factors affecting their processability and electrical performance. This study explored the relationship between the melt index of grafted polypropylene and its high-temperature electrical performance. As the melt index increased, the high-temperature breakdown field strength and energy storage characteristics initially decreased and then improved. Through mass production on a BOPP film production line, it was found that samples with a melt index above 4 could not be continuously produced. Considering both film processability and high-temperature electrical performance, adjusting the melt index of grafted polypropylene to 2.9 was deemed optimal. This study provides technical support for the production of high-performance grafted polypropylene capacitor films.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Conducted and Irradiated Signals for PD Pattern Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This research study aims to investigate the influence of various partial discharge (PD) sensors in handling PD signals separations. Two PD sources have been used to generate surface partial discharges. Surface partial discharges were generated using two PD sources, and the signals were detected using three different sensors: a High-Frequency Current Transformer (HFCT), a resistor (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</inf>), and a VHF antenna. The primary objective is to highlight the strengths and challenges associated with each PD sensor, particularly in the context of signal separation and clustering. The impact of the characteristics of the selected sensors is examined. The study evaluates the efficiency, potential, and limitations of the sensor-clustering algorithm sets to evaluate the possibilities in employing them for fault detection and maintenance planning.

articleTitle: Influence of Rise Time on the Aging of Electric Machine Windings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This study examines how fast rise times, which are common in modern power electronics and drive systems, affect the aging of electric machine windings. It focuses on how to ensure these windings can last longer and work reliably in electrical systems. A twisted pair magnet wire with insulation commonly used in wound machines was used to get experimental data to understand how different voltage waveforms can influence endurance testing of motor insulation systems powered by inverters. Unlike past studies that looked at comparatively slower rise times and fewer repetitions, this research specifically addresses the challenges posed by next-generation wide bandgap (WBG)-based conversion systems. These systems operate at very high speeds, up to 100 kV/μs, and switch frequencies up to 500 kHz, where both frequency and rise time are crucial factors affecting insulation aging over time.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Aluminum and Brass Electrodes in Laser Induced Pressure Pulse Method: Effects on Signal Strength
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This study aims to enhance the efficiency of the Laser Induced Pressure Pulse (LIPP) method, focusing on comparing the effect of different electrode metals. Results show significant differences in signal strength between brass and aluminum electrodes. The higher acoustic impedance of brass resulted in less induction of the laser-generated shock wave inside the sample, leading to a smaller charge signal. This shows the importance of choosing the electrode material for LIPP application. Aluminum was shown to be more suitable for achieving higher signal peaks.

articleTitle: PFAS-Free Ablative Insulation for Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is a critical element of gas breaker insulation due to its tendency to ablate into an insulating gas rather than char and degrade. However, PTFE is a type of per-and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS), materials which are gradually being phased out due to environmental and health concerns. This has led to a series of replacements which are themselves PFAS materials and thus also concerning. As such, it is critical to find PFAS-free alternatives for PTFE in this application, particularly ones that replicate its ability to ablate and form a quenching vapor. Here, alternatives for PTFE insulation for switchgears were investigated for their thermal and electrical stability. The materials of choice were Delrin, Nylon, and LDPE. In this work, these commercially available materials were studied as a baseline for future work involving a chloro-polymer-based composite material. Thermal stability was examined via thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and electrical stability was examined via arc tracking resistance measurements. Delrin behaved the most similarly to PTFE in terms of arc tracking by not charring, though it was much less thermally stable, degrading at much lower temperatures. Additionally, these alternative polymer materials were directly compared to PTFE and an alumina reference in a small-scale ablation test. Delrin ablated the most readily under these conditions and had multiple ablation events from a single arc. It also caused the largest increase in arc voltage due to the insulating gas it generated, making it the most effective at absorbing the arc's energy.

articleTitle: Electric Field Analysis at Triple-Joints and Localized Defects on Different Composite Insulators Designs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Composite insulators have been extensively employed around the world due to their lighter weight, improved performance in harsh environments, and potential lower maintenance costs. However, brittle fracture caused by stress corrosion cracking may occur due to water penetration into metal end fittings during operation, even under lower mechanical loads, possibly leading to a complete failure of the composite insulator. Given that the electric field may play a role in brittle fracture of composite insulators in form of partial discharges, two of the most common existing designs that result in different locations of the triple-joint - interface consisting of metal end-fitting, air, and polymer - are studied. The electric field intensification at the triple-joints is modeled using finite element modeling and validated by analytical calculations. In addition, as another recurrent physical defect in composite insulators, air voids are assessed in different locations of the analyzed composite insulator designs to determine their criticality on brittle fracture mechanism. Results present the optimal design based on the location of the triple-joint in composite insulators, and the most critical locations where air voids may severely contribute to failure modes in the composite insulators.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Oxygen-Related Radical Effects on Aramid Surface Modification via Vacuum Ultraviolet Photolysis Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Understanding the interaction mechanisms between plasma components, particularly oxygen-related radicals, and polymers is crucial for guiding industrial applications. This study employs a novel vacuum ultraviolet photolysis reactive species (VUV PRS) method to quantitatively introduce active reactants to aramid surfaces. The modified aramid samples were characterized under various treatment parameters and durations using water contact angle (WCA) measurements and attenuated total reflection-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATRFTIR). Our findings reveal that the surface reaction rate is linearly correlated with the density of O/H radicals, with limited effects brought by OH, HO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. The reactions include the formation of OH graft structures and the cleavage of amide bonds. This research provides theoretical insights for the oxygencontaining plasma treatment of polymers.

articleTitle: Dielectric Properties of Polypropylene/Polystyrene Blends
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Polyolefins are currently used as electric insulators in engineering applications. Blending polymers is one of the ways to obtain materials with enhanced specific properties such as electrical, mechanical or rheological properties. Usually polymers are immiscible together, thus the resulting properties are directly related to microstructure of the blends. In this paper, the dielectric properties of polypropylene (PP) and polystyrene (PS), two immiscible polymers and their blends, were investigated at a range of concentration where these two polymers form a co-continuous structure where one of the polymer percolates through the other one, and at lower concentration of the minor (or dispersed) phase where it can form a droplet-type structure, the minor phase being embedded into the matrix of the major (or dispersing) phase. The purpose is then to determine the evolution of the electrical properties according to the amount of each polymer involved in the blend in order to determine the best ratio for specific applications.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation on the Bubbling Inception Temperature in Kraft Paper Impregnated with Mineral Oil and Synthetic Ester
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper aims to comprehensively investigate the Bubbling Inception Temperature (BIT) of two insulating fluids. The reason why the BIT is important is that it is a critical parameter to estimate the bubble formation within power transformers during overload conditions. Indeed, with the ever-increasing demand of electricity, transformer overload could be a source of bubble unfolding. The study specifically focuses on Kraft paper impregnated with a mineral oil and a synthetic ester. A specially-designed experimental setup that helps controlling key parameters such as temperature and moisture content, is employed to investigate the BIT. The investigations reveal that the BIT of synthetic ester-impregnated paper is higher than that of mineral oil-impregnated paper. The present study provides valuable insights to prevent bubble formation and enhance the overall reliability of power transformers.

articleTitle: Simulation of Space Charge Behavior in Silicone Gel Above Edge Termination Area of Power Chip
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In recent years, IGBT modules have been required to ensure high reliability under severe environment with high temperature and high humidity. During the reliability test, space charge injected from electrodes accumulates in the encapsulating resin above edge termination of IGBT chips. Then, the space charge distorts the electric field distribution inside the chips, potentially could lead to failures such as increase of leakage current. Therefore, it is important to understand the space charge distribution in resin for more reliable IGBT design. In this study, we investigated the space charge distribution of the silicone gel on the high voltage IGBT chip using TCAD simulation and discussed its effects on electrical properties of the device.

articleTitle: Effect of TiO2Particle Shape and Deformation Rate on Permittivity of Silicone Elastomer Composite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The power generation output of a dielectric elastomer (DE) energy harvesting device can be enhanced by increasing the permittivity of the DE sheet. It has already been confirmed that the permittivity of the DE sheet can be increased by filling it with high-permittivity particles, but the permittivity of the DE sheet shows a stretch dependence, i.e., decreasing when the DE sheet is stretched. Moreover, the effect of the particle shape (aspect ratio) on the stretch-dependent permittivity of DE sheet is unclear. In this study, we filled the silicone rubber sheets by TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>particles with high and low aspect ratio, respectively, and the relative permittivities of them were measured under different stretch state. Then the effective permittivity of DE sheet filled with rod-like particles was calculated by using finite-element method. The DE sheet filled with TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>particles (high aspect ratio) has a high permittivity, while due to the alignment of the particles, it shows a high decrease rate in the permittivity when it is stretched, which in turn results in a decrease of power generation output. The power generation output cannot be further improved compared with the DE sheet filled with TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> particles with low aspect ratio.

articleTitle: Basic Study on Effect of Corrugated Barrier Structure Made Using 3D-Printer on Surface Discharge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Creeping discharge of high voltage apparatuses, such as insulators and bushings, were suppressed using barriers on the insulation surface for miniaturization and high reliability. A more complex structure of insulation resin is possible due to the development of three-dimensional (3D) printing. More effective barrier structures for suppressing creeping discharge can be fabricated using this technology. Therefore, insulation structures by 3D printing are expected to be widely applied to high voltage apparatuses. We evaluated the partial discharge voltage (PDIV) and the flashover voltage (FOV) on the surface of insulation fabricated by 3D printing. A corrugated surface barrier was 0.5 mm in height and interval, but the widths differed, i.e., 0.5 and 1.0 mm. The PDIV and FOV on the surfaces were evaluated compared with the reference sample without the barrier structure. We found that the PDIV was higher as the sample with a large barrier width and the FOV of the sample with a barrier width of 0.5mm was highest. The findings of this study will contribute to customize the insulation characteristics according to an insulation design.

articleTitle: Discussion on the Defects in HVDC Cables and Their Relation with the Occurrence of Partial Discharge Phenomena
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Extruded cables for high voltage (HV) applications, particularly for HVDC systems, must be manufactured to a high standard to ensure their quality and design life. Any deficiencies or imperfections during the manufacturing processes can lead to defects that negatively impact the performance of the final product during operation. There are methods available to detect weaknesses both through end-of-line tests and continuous monitoring of the assets. One innovative diagnostic technique gaining recognition in the HVDC cable industry is Partial Discharge Analysis (PDA). This technique can identify prospective defects early on, preventing accelerated degradation of the insulation material, and potentially leading the cable system to failure. This paper discusses some of the various types of defects that can arise in cables due to poor manufacturing practices, as well as during their operational lifespan, and the corresponding types of PD phenomena that may occur. Examples of imperfections will be presented, debating their probability of occurrence based on the manufacturing processes and materials, and their associated PD signals when exposed to DC electrical fields. Most of the samples used in the investigation originate and have been collected in the ongoing activities within the NEWGEN project, which is fully funded by the European Union Grant Agreement No.101075592.

articleTitle: PEA Measurement on 525kV HVDC Cable Compliant with IEEE 1732 Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In 2017, IEEE proposed a procedure to evaluate the effect of space charge accumulation in extruded cables for HVDC applications with rated voltages up to 550kV. In this paper, the results of a measurement performed with the Pulsed Electro-Acoustic (PEA) method are reported, according to the guidelines of the IEEE recommendation. The measurement has been performed on a full-size cable with rated voltage of 525kV. The procedure involves a phase of positive volt-on (U0) and volt-off and another of negative volt-on (-U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) and volt-off. The results show that both in the positive volt-on phase (lasting 9 hours) and in the negative volt-on phase (lasting 6 hours), the electric field profile underwent an inversion process. Having performed a continuous acquisition of the charge profile, it was observed that the inversion occurs in both cases during the first hour. While the stabilization of the field profile occurred first in the negative volt-on phase.

articleTitle: Effect of Moisture and Load Change on Clamping Pressure in a Transformer Test Rig
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: During the manufacturing of a power transformer, typically, a fixed clamping pressure is exerted on the winding structure to keep its mechanical integrity during short circuit faults. Various factors, e.g., breathing during load cycles, poor sealing, aging of cellulose materials, etc., introduce moisture in the transformer during its long service life. A typical power transformer operation has a continuous moisture exchange between the cellulose material and the oil. The pressboard samples and controllable heated brass plates are stacked in a test rig. This paper investigates the effect of moisture and load variation on the development of clamping pressure in the test rig. Pressboard samples with two different moisture contents are studied: dry (~0.6%) and wet (~4.7%). Two different heating cycles are investigated: a constant load and a frequent start-stop load. The temperature of the brass plate and oil, relative humidity of oil and pressboard, and clamping force are measured throughout the experiment. It has been observed that the clamping pressure follows the temperature profile of the brass plates. A significant loss of clamping pressure is observed after mounting the wet samples in the rig. The clamping pressure drops further after the first heating cycle as the rig temperature returns to the ambient. However, when the rig returns to room temperature, there is no noticeable decrease in clamping pressure, neither for the dry sample nor for the wet sample after its first heating cycle.

articleTitle: Effect of Thermal Treatment with High DC Stress on the Conductivity in Imide-Based Insulating Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper evaluates the leakage current properties of polyimide and polyamide-imide with two different pretreatments. Recently, with the spread of electric vehicles, there has been a demand to maintain the performance of insulating materials used for the winding coating of motors in these vehicles under high temperatures and high electric fields. However, it has already been clear that when high DC voltages are applied to some polymeric insulating materials under high temperatures for a long time, dielectric breakdown occurs, and it is assumed that the breakdown is due to distortion of the internal electric field caused by the accumulation of space charge and an increase in leakage current. However, the insulation degradation phenomena leading to dielectric breakdown have not yet been fully understood. This study evaluated the current leakage characteristics of polyimide and polyamide-imide films under three different conditions: untreated, thermally treated, and electrothermal treated, using the direct current integrated charge method (DCIC-Q(t)). The results show no significant change was observed in polyimide. Meanwhile, polyamide-imide showed insulation degradation due to the electrothermal treatment.

articleTitle: A Study of Transient Electric Field Distribution of XLPE Cable Joint in a VSC-HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cable is one of the key assets in a voltage source converter (VSC) based high-voltage direct current (HVDC) system. Due to the complex geometry and interfaces among different material, cable joints are the most critical part of a cable system. In this paper, two typical transient overvoltages (zero-crossing damped overvoltage, very slow front overvoltage) is obtained in a VSC-HVDC system and their effects on the electric field distribution of the joint insulation is investigated. The results are compared with the standard switching impulse tests. The temperature-dependent and electric field-dependent characteristics of insulation conductivity and the ratio of double-layer material conductivities at the joint interface are discussed. It is found that geometry of the cable joint and the ratio of XLPE and ethylene propylene diene monomer (EPDM) conductivities are the dominant factors on both steady-state DC field and transient electric fields caused by the system overvoltage.

articleTitle: Analysis of Defects and Noise in Cast-Resin Transformers Using UHF Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Cast-resin transformers have a risk of accidents leading to dielectric breakdown due to manufacturing defects such as cracks, thermal aging and voids. Detecting manufacturing defects and degradation in advance to prevent accidents is crucial in PD research. However, not only discharge caused by defects but also noise signals can be introduced through sensors. Therefore, it is necessary to study UPS noise that can be enter through sensors installed in cast-resin transformers. In this paper, the signals of defects and noise were measured and derived into PRPD patterns. The defects were selected as corona, surface and void discharges, and the noise sources were the rectifier and inverter of the UPS. It was confirmed that PRPD patterns differ according to the type of defect. Additionally, corona discharge showed pattern changes over time, while surface discharge extinguished. UPS noise varies depending on the operation of the rectifier and inverter. Through this, it is possible to distinguish between defects and noise.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Dual-Temperature Aging Method for the Electrical Insulation System of Direct Oil-Cooled Motors in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: It is very essential to qualify the impact of the automatic transmission fluid (ATF) to the electrical insulation system (EIS) of direct oil-cooled motors, with the development of electrification trends in the automotive industry and prevalence of direct oil cooling in electric powertrains. This study performed the dual-temperature aging test to evaluate the ATF impacts on the motorettes: one motorette was submerged in the ATF, and the other was exposed to ATF vapor. Both of them flowed through the same current, and generated heat via the Joule effect to simulate the direct oil-cooled motor operation. The temperature of the ATF was controlled at 100°C during the high-temperature (200°C) aging process. The results show that the ATF vapor significantly reduced the reliability of the EIS. Additionally, the properties of the ATF were analyzed before and after aging. A possible aging mechanism of the motorettes under ATF conditions was discussed. The result also suggests that the dual-temperature aging method provides more comprehensive information than the traditional oven tests, enhancing a better understanding of the effects of the lubricating oil, additives, etc., on the EIS of direct oil-cooled motors.

articleTitle: Annealing Effect with High DC Stress in Epoxy Resin on Insulating Degradation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper evaluates the insulation performance change of acid anhydride epoxy resins when subjected to annealing and annealing with DC stress. In this increasingly electrified society, the evolution of power conversion technology is essential. Power modules are critical devices used for power conversion, and they are known to generate heat due to Joule heat during operation. Therefore, insulating materials used in power modules are also required to exhibit high insulation performance at high temperatures under electric fields. However, epoxy resins, which are expected to be used for the insulating material, are known to accumulate space charge in such conditions, being worried about decreasing insulation performance. However, this degradation has not yet been fully studied. Therefore, this paper evaluates the leakage current measurement of epoxy resin using a current integrated charge method, the so-called Q(t) method. At first, since a relatively high voltage is applied to the epoxy sample at a high temperature in the Q(t) measurement, it is found that such a voltage application induces an improvement in the insulating performance of the sample. However, when the high voltage was applied to the sample at a higher temperature after the Q(t) measurement, it was found that there was an apparent insulating degradation in the sample. In contrast, such degradation was not observed after annealing without the voltage application. Therefore, we concluded that insulating degradation was induced in the electric field at high temperatures.

articleTitle: Dielectric Gradient Materials Fabrication: A Synergy of Electric Field Assistance and Photocuring 3D Printing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This study explores the impact of applying an electric field during the photocuring 3D printing process on the final properties of the printed products. Photocuring 3D printing is a layer-by-layer technique where the resin transitions from a liquid to a solid state upon exposure to ultraviolet (UV) light, thereby providing the conditions for the orientation and alignment of filler particles. In this research, an alternating current (AC) electric field was introduced during the printing process. The high dielectric filler particles within the resin experienced dielectrophoresis, resulting in their orientation and alignment. Due to the orthogonal anisotropy of their dielectric constants, the dielectric constant increased in the direction of the electric field and decreased perpendicularly, with dielectric loss following a similar trend. This study demonstrates the feasibility of embedding electrodes in the photocuring 3D printing process. Future work could explore the effects of different electric field properties and electrode shapes on the gradient materials produced by photocuring 3D printing, offering new insights into optimizing the properties of printed materials through controlled electric field application.

articleTitle: Conductive Atomic Force Microscopy to Shed New Light on Surface Electrical Trees
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Greenhouse gas emission reduction is underway worldwide to mitigate the effects of global warming. Among the new initiatives, electrification of passenger airplanes could yield enormous economic and environmental benefits although a few key technology barriers remain. One main challenge is related to the insulation system. This is because insulation systems required for electric aircraft will need to withstand higher local electric fields and higher temperatures. Unfortunately, all polymeric insulation systems are subject to an aging degradation mechanism called electrical treeing, which can lead to electrical breakdown. The defect is exacerbated in areas of local high field, making it a crucial issue to understand in aircraft insulation. While this mode of tree-aging has been studied for centuries, the mechanism has been debated in the literature. Using new characterization techniques to shed new light on parts of the electrical treeing mechanism is key to new understanding that can lead to mitigation solution. One such new characterization technique is conductive atomic force microscopy (c-AFM). By using a conductive tip on the AFM, the electrical tree can be studied with respect to the electrical conductance of the interior walls and their speculated contribution to electrical tree propagation. This work used c-AFM to study an electrical tree on the surface of an insulation material to establish a baseline procedure in using this technique to study the walls of electrical trees. It was found that the c-AFM can provide conductivity results within and around an electrical tree.

articleTitle: Structural Alteration and Electric Field Estimation Inside HVAC Cable due to Inhomogeneous Aging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Under diverse loading conditions, high-voltage alternating current (HV-AC) underground polymeric cables exhibit a radial temperature gradient and experience differential thermal stress, resulting in inhomogeneous aging of the polymeric material. Consequently, a differential localized structural alterations occur at different radial positions within the insulation bulk of the cable. To investigate these effects, the authors have examined the cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) insulation taken from HV-AC cables. Using a lathe machine, samples were extracted and subjected to various tests. The findings revealed significant variations in the morphology of the XLPE layers at different radial positions within the cable insulation bulk. These effects were further investigated by measuring the permittivity of samples extracted from different radial positions within the insulation bulk. The permittivity data is then fitted to field, temperature and radial position dependent equation, and the AC electric field distribution is estimated. The findings are also corroborated by AC breakdown tests.

articleTitle: Analysis of Partial Discharge Characteristics of MVDC Power Cables Optimally Designed for All-Electric Wide Body Aircraft Under Varying Pressure During Takeoff and Descent
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Introducing all-electric aircraft (AEA) is a viable option to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the aviation sector. The wide-body AEA's electric power system needs higher voltage levels (a few kVs) than the voltage levels of existing aircraft cables. Consequently, the aircraft cable insulation needs to withstand higher voltage, maintaining low mass since the EPS contributes about 30% of the total mass of aircraft. Aircraft cables face several challenges: arcing, partial discharge (PD), and electromagnetic interference due to low-pressure environments at high altitudes. Several multilayer insulation designs for aircraft cables were proposed to overcome these challenges, and the optimized fabrication process of these cables was presented in our previous works. This paper analyzes the PD characteristics of fabricated flat insulation samples for the cables under different air pressures as the aircraft operates from 1 atm at the time of takeoff to 18.8 kPa at the typical cruising altitude (12.2 km).

articleTitle: Investigating Partial Discharge Characteristics in Silicone Gel for (U)WBG Power Modules Under Negative DC Voltage: A Comparative Study of Optical and Electrical Detection Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper aims to investigate the accuracy of the optical partial discharge (PD) detection technique in recording PD activity within silicone gel (SG), using conventional electrical techniques as a reference. Given the inevitable high-frequency, high-slew rate square voltage operation of (U)WBG power modules, alternative PD measurement techniques are needed to replace conventional electrical methods. Before implementing optical detection for high-slew rate square pulses, its accuracy under DC voltage conditions-where electrical PD detection is reliable due to its immunity to EMI and disturbances-must be assessed. This study analyzes PD activity within SG using a needle-to-plate electrode configuration under varying negative DC voltages, employing both optical and electrical PD detection techniques. It also examines the impact of decreasing the distance between the electrodes and compares PD signal results at various voltages between the APD optical sensor and the Omicron MPD800 software. As no previous research has correlated electrical and optical PD detection methods, this paper serves as a valuable reference for future studies involving PD measurement in encapsulation materials under high-frequency, high-slew rate square wave voltages.

articleTitle: Tracking Electron and Hole Trap Densities on Commercial Display Glass
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Surface charges can cause problems in industry dealing with high voltage applications. In current literature, charge measurements on glass surfaces are lacking. Furthermore, no operando measurements on these charges can be performed, due to the invasiveness of the available diagnostics. In this research, an operando measurement technique, based on the Pockels effect is introduced that can be applied to glass (among other dielectrics). Furthermore, an electrostatic voltmeter is used for surface potential measurements on commercial display glass in open air. Surface charge deposition is done using an X-ray ionizer. Subsequently, the decay of the surface potential, induced by the surface charges, is translated to trap density using the isothermal surface potential decay model. The energy distribution is shown to be comparable for electron and hole traps with a peak at approximately ~0.88 eV and 0.89 eV respectively. However, the surface charge spreading is observed to be faster for negative charges. The energy and density of traps cannot be assessed yet with Pockels, because of low sensitivity, while the time and spatial resolution of the proposed method are potentially better than existing techniques.

articleTitle: Compositional Properties and High Field Electrical Conduction of PECVD Silicon Nitride Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The composition of silicon nitride (SiNx) films, varying from N-rich to Si-rich stoichiometries, significantly impacts their structural and electrical properties. In this study, we investigate the composition dependent characteristics of amorphous SiNx films, deposited by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD), using electron microprobe microscopy (EMP), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), secondary ion mass spectroscopy (SIMS), and high-voltage broadband dielectric spectroscopy (HVBDS). It is found that amorphous PECVD SiNx films contain hydrogen bonded to both Si and N atoms, in the form of Si-H and N-H bonds, which vary with the ratio x=[N]/[Si] of SiNx. These films exhibit a wide range of electrical conduction properties such that the low frequency HVBDS is a powerful technique that clearly reveals the structural transition from N-rich to Si-rich types of SiNx films. We present and discuss the influence of the Si-N bonding structure and the hydrogenation process on the low frequency AC conductivity based on different SiNx ratios.

articleTitle: Simulating Reverse Electrical Trees Using Kinetic Model and Cellular Automata
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Electric treeing is a mechanism of failure in solid polymeric insulations. Under some conditions, trees grow through filamentary trees, which have a small diameter and do not cause breakdown when they reach the counter-electrode. In this case, reverse trees grow opposite to the forward-filamentary tree. Several methods are available to model electric trees and their phenomenology. Among them is the kinetic model, which proposes that electric trees grow due to microfractures present in the material. This model had previously been considered to model tree growth, but we extended it to include the widening of tree branches in a prior study. In this work, we included the phenomenology of reverse trees and their relationship with filamentary trees. The simulation showed that filamentary trees grow until they are close to the counter-electrode, and when reverse trees begin to form, their branches widen. From this point, filamentary trees do not grow, but branches widen until the current density is high enough for final dielectric breakdown.

articleTitle: An Accelerated Testing Framework for Assessing the DC Erosion Resistance of Silicone Rubber Composites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper studies the use of an accelerated and controllable testing framework to asses the DC erosion resistance of silicone rubber composites used for high voltage outdoor insulation applications. The framework examines the use of repeatable testing methods that generate controlled dry-band arcing under wet and dry conditions using a modified DC setup of the Comparative Tracking Index test and the AC dry-arc resistance test respectively. The composites are tested under the DC Inclined Plane Tracking-Erosion test with the outcomes used as reference for the composites' DC erosion resistance. With respect to the DC Inclined Plane test, the results indicate similar erosion resistance outcomes to the accelerated tests with a more distinct variance in the outcomes under the DC Comparative Tracking Index test. Moreover, a distinct pattern for the leakage current waveforms are observed amongst the composites under the DC Comparative Tracking Index test which correlates with the DC erosion resistance outcomes. The outcomes of the accelerated tests are repeatable, controllable and thus provide low uncertainty in the measurements for assessing the erosion resistance of silicone rubber. These observations could be utilized within the proposed accelerated framework to supplement the DC Inclined Plane Tracking-Erosion test in assessing the DC erosion resistance of silicone rubber composites for outdoor insulation applications.

articleTitle: Synergistic Aging of Silicone Rubber by Wet/Dry Heat and Silicone Grease
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The interface of cable joints formed by cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) and silicone rubber (SR) are not only affected by the temperature, but also by moisture and silicone grease (SG). In this paper, the synergies effects of moisture, heat and SG on the insulating properties of SR in cable joint is investigated. The aging experiment of SR were carried out. Molecular dynamics simulation was carried out to study the influence mechanism of SG, temperature and humidity on the structure of SR. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and Raman spectroscopy were used to study the microstructure of the materials. XPS shows that SG reduces the free volume of SR and provides more cross-linking sites, which promotes the oxidative cross-linking reactions on the surface of SR at high temperatures. Therefore, the hardened inorganic layer appears on the surface of the specimen. What's more, the Raman spectroscopy result shows that the high temperature promotes the swelling caused by SG, which destroys the internal cross-linking network of the specimen and breaks the polymer chains. The mechanism of internal and surface deterioration of SR are different, but SG and dry/humid heat environment play a joint role in the aging of SR.

articleTitle: Field Experience of Sampling and Laboratory Analyses of C4-FN/CO2 Insulating Gas Mixture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Utilities have installed non-SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> gas blends in gas insulated switchgear (GIS) as a step towards Net Zero. The present work attempts to investigate the stability of fluoronitrile (C4-FN, CAS No. 42532-60-5) based insulating gas blend in power asset. Field experience of sampling procedure of 4% C4-FN / 96% CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas blend from gas zones in an operational 400 kV GIS substation is presented. Samples were analyzed using Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS) and Fourier Transform - Infrared Spectroscopy (FT-IR) at three different labs. The results indicate minimal formation of decomposition by-products showing the gas blend is relatively stable within the operational range and during the period of its use in gas zones.

articleTitle: A Mechanism of Space Charge Formation in Silicone Gel and its Effect to Instability of High Voltage Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: When the IGBT and diode devices are kept in turn-off state, the collector-emitter leakage current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{I}_{\text{ce}})$</tex> is very small initially, however it could increase suddenly after a certain time and result in avalanche breakdown failure depending on the environment such as temperature, humidity, and process conditions. In this paper, the mechanism of this <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{\text{ce}}$</tex> instability of high voltage power devices is investigated in relation to space charge in silicone gel encapsulation material covering the chips. It is shown that the instability depends on the height of emitter bonding wire which run through above the surface of the edge termination area of the chip. The lower the height, the sooner the initiation of the sudden increase of the Ice occurred, indicating the electric field in silicone gel below the emitter wires is a major factor of the instability. Space charge in silicone gel sheet was measured by PEA (Pulsed Electro Acoustic) method. The large density of negative charge was observed in the silicone gel sheet with aluminum electrodes while the charge density of the sample with Au electrodes is an order of magnitude lower. The electrode material dependence indicates the origin of the charge is electrons injected from Al since the work function of Al is smaller than that of Au. Furthermore, the conduction current of the silicone gel sheet with Al electrodes was far larger than that with Au electrodes. These results strongly support that the origin of the space charge is electrons injected from the surface of aluminum wires.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Thermally Aged and Gamma-Irradiated Nuclear Cables using Electrical Diagnostic Tests
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Electrical cables are essential within nuclear power plants (NPPs) to support power, control, and instrumentation systems. Given the importance of these systems in servicing NPPs, prevention and detection of electrical cable failure is a vital part of aging management programs. As such, nondestructive examination (NDE) techniques are commonly used to evaluate the degradation of electrical cables. Common offline electrical NDE techniques for condition monitoring (CM) may include lowfrequency dielectric spectroscopy (LFDS), time domain reflectometry (TDR), frequency domain reflectometry (FDR), and time domain dielectric spectroscopy (TDDS). However, there is no single NDE method to comprehensively evaluate cable condition and, in many cases, a combination of local and global tests is required. In this work, we evaluate the sequentially applied thermal and gamma radiation aging of electrical cable insulation using electrical diagnostic test methods to better understand damage detection in cables using a combination approach. Gamma radiation aging was performed on cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) polymer cable insulation material commonly used in NPPs. Long “30-foot” cable mandrels of XLPE were irradiated at room temperature, using Co-60 gamma-rays, to intervals of 100 kGy each, for a combined total dose of 500 kGy. Post irradiation electrical testing was performed on these cables. Preliminary results of the electrical diagnostics indicate trends with increasing aging conditions in the XLPE cable insulation samples. The results of this study advance electrical-based diagnostic techniques for condition monitoring of electrical cables in NPPs, providing plant operators with more complete information to support repair, mitigation, or replacement decisions.

articleTitle: 3D SSTDR Digital Twin of an Electrical Cable: A First Glance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Nuclear power plant (NPP) electrical cables are essential components of power, control, and instrumentation systems. Environmental stressors, such as heat and radiation, can reduce electrical cable service life. Electrical reflectometry methods are commonly employed to identify and locate cable degradation. However, most reflectometry methods require cables to be de-energized and de-terminated prior to testing. Spread spectrum time domain reflectometry (SSTDR) has been identified as a potential solution to these issues but additional work is needed to understand the influence of a wide variety of fault types on SSTDR response. In this work, we explore development a fully 3D SSTDR digital twin to predict cable degradation. A typical 3-conductor low-voltage electrical cable was selected for evaluation and 20-m of cable was simulated within COMSOL Multiphysics<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>, Insulation damage was induced over 1-m through scaling of empirically-derived permittivity. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the approach to accurately detecting cable damage but additional work is needed to reduce noise due to the connection.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Discharge State Recognition for Optical Partial Discharge Signal Induced by Metal Particles in Gas Insulated Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The assessment of operational risk in gas-insulated equipment can be effectively achieved by identifying the evolution status of defect-induced discharges. However, existing methods are often hindered by electromagnetic noise, which complicates the accurate identification of the intricate discharge features associated with defects. To address this issue, we propose a partial discharge (PD) pattern recognition method based on photon counting features. This approach aims to mitigate the impact of electromagnetic noise and improve the accuracy of defect-induced discharge identification. Furthermore, the discussion of phase-resolved photon counting (PRPC) patterns under the influence of defects is completed, from which we extract feature parameters for quantifying discharge evolution. Subsequently, a clustering strategy to establish a model for recognizing discharge states is proposed. Findings not only contribute to an enhanced understanding of the complex luminescence phenomena related to PD evolution but also offer new perspectives for analyzing defect-induced discharge states.

articleTitle: Low Permittivity Porous Polymer Composites for High PDIV Electrical Insulation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In response to the increasing power demands in modern aircraft, insulation materials must ensure exceptional performance and reliability, while withstanding higher voltage levels. To maintain reasonable material thicknesses, one approach is to increase the Partial Discharge Inception Voltage (PDIV) by reducing the permittivity of the insulation materials. This strategy involves introducing inorganic porous fillers into the polymer matrix. Flat PEKK samples were prepared by incorporating 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 vol.% of porous silica-based fillers in a dried powder form. After thorough mixing, the samples were pressed at high temperatures. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) revealed no significant variations in the thermal properties of the composites. Dielectric characterizations demonstrated a marked improvement in permittivity, particularly at low temperatures and under medium to high frequencies at elevated temperatures. These findings were corroborated by PDIV measurements and simulations, which indicated a substantial increase in the threshold voltage. However, as expected, the breakdown strength decreased with the addition of the micro-inorganic fillers. The improvements in permittivity and PDIV are promising, suggesting that these composites could be further explored for industrial applications, particularly in assessing their processing and insulation performance within complete systems.

articleTitle: Dynamic Conductivity Processes in Glass-Filled Polyimide Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Assessments of the risk of electrostatic discharge (ESD) due to spacecraft charging require knowledge of materials' conductivity in flight-like conditions. Due to the difficulty in measuring and modeling conductivity in space conditions, it is common to conservatively assume the minimum steady-state dark conductivity. This study investigates impacts of charging rate, temperature, electric field, and time on the dynamic conductivity of glass-filled polyimide circuit board materials. The chargestorage method of measuring conductivity was used on samples mounted on a cold plate in vacuum. Charging was performed incrementally with conductivity measured between electron exposures. Beam ramp down conditions were varied to investigate the impact of charging rate on the observed charge decay. Observed conductivity does not appear to depend on the rate of beam shut off. Conductivity does depend strongly on electric field, time, and temperature. These effects typically are studied separately.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation on Breakdown Characteristics of High Temperature CO2 Gas Using Inductively Coupled Thermal Plasma System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Dielectric strength in high temperature gas is crucial to determine the success or failure of current interruption in a gas circuit breaker. We aim to experimentally clarify the dielectric properties of high temperature gases. In our research, a unique method using inductively coupled thermal plasmas (ICTP) was applied to elevate the temperature of insulation gases. The breakdown voltage (BDV) in high-temperature CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas was measured, with the temperature controlled by adjusting the ICTP parameters. To verify the measured experimental results, a theoretical calculation of reduced electric field by solving the Boltzmann equation was also performed. As a result, the BDV significantly decreased at the temperatures above 5500 K, with the change in appearance of discharge. This is because, in this temperature range, the gas composition changes from CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> molecule to CO molecule and O atom dissociated, thereby changing the particles that dominate the breakdown.

articleTitle: Electrical Tree Growth at Various Needle-Plane Distances Under Constant HVDC Voltages in Flexible Epoxy Resins
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In high-voltage systems, electrical insulation is essential for safety operation including isolation from ground potential, and its failure will cause the entire high voltage system to fail. Metallic protrusions in the insulation concentrate the electric field strength and provide conditions for electrical tree initiation and growth, which may lead to unexpected premature insulation failure. In this work, electrical treeing growth in flexible epoxy resins has been investigated using controlled geometry metallic protrusions in the form of needles cast in epoxy resin. The electrical tree experiments were conducted with a constant High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) voltage without any repetitive interruptions in the HVDC supply or superimposed AC waveforms. The influence of variations in the pin-plane distances on the electrical tree inception and growth were examined. The magnitude of partial discharges with respect to the time of inception and tree growth duration were measured and analyzed. The partial discharge measurements were matched to superimposed photographs of the electrical trees growth to aid understanding of the electrical treeing progress under HVDC applied stresses.

articleTitle: Dielectric Response of Insulating Film for Lithium-Ion Battery Over Broad Ranges of Frequency and Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Li-ion batteries have been introduced into high voltage energy storage, and the insulating film of battery may be exposed to overvoltage from transmission lines. Therefore, the dielectric properties of insulating film should be carefully studied. In this research, the dielectric response of insulating film over broad ranges of frequency and temperature is investigated. The contributions of three loss peak polarization processes are decoupled based on Dissado-Hill model. The temperature dependence of loss peak is studied by two different approaches, and the activation characteristic is revealed accordingly. The distinction between activation energies indicates the difference of relaxation type.

articleTitle: Polypropylene Copolymers and Blends for HVDC Cable Insulation: Initial Characterization and Pilot-scale Production
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper introduces a preliminary characterization of polypropylene-based copolymers as well as a possible ternary blend as a candidate to be used for HVDC cable insulation in the framework of the European project NEWGEN (New GENeration of HVDC insulating materials, cables and systems). The effect of production process scale-up (from mini-scale to pilot-scale cast-processing) is also investigated for the promising PP ternary blend which is essentially composed of homophasic PP random copolymer (RACO), heterophasic PP copolymer (HECO), and propylene-based elastomer (PBE). The preliminary dielectric characterization introduces a promising RACO/HECO/PBE blend with a similar and comparable performance of mini-scale and up-scaled specimens. Mechanical characterization show that incorporating HECO and PBE in the ternary blend reduces the stiffness metrics of RACO towards suitable values for HVDC cable applications.

articleTitle: Observation of Polymeric Insulator Deterioration Due to Local Arc Discharges
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Silicone rubber, commonly used as the housing material for polymer insulators, undergoes surface degradation, such as erosion, when exposed to local arc discharges. Investigating the progression of this degradation is crucial for understanding the aging characteristics of polymer insulators and evaluating their remaining service life. In this study, we conducted a saltwater dripping test to efficiently induce local arc discharges by dripping saltwater onto polymer insulators under alternating current voltage. We observed significant surface degradation phenomena, including surface roughening and erosion. These observations are essential for understanding the aging process of polymer insulators and for developing methods to evaluate their remaining service life.

articleTitle: Electret Charge Stability in Meltblown Polypropylene Fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In the present work charge storage in meltblown polypropylene (PP) fibers has been investigated by means of thermally stimulated surface potential decay. It has been shown that a surface chemical treatment of fibers or, alternatively, polymer granules prior to extrusion, leads to a significant improvement of the electret charge stability. We attribute this to the formation of new deeper traps in the material resulting from the chemical treatment with the phosphoric acid. The results obtained offer a new approach to improve efficiency and charge stability of meltblown electrostatic filters.

articleTitle: Breakdown Performance of CO2, Technical Air, and Technical Air with 7.5% C5-Fluoroketone in a Weakly Nonuniform Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In the search for alternatives to SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> in gas insulated switchgears, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, technical air (80% N2, 20% O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), and technical air with small admixtures such as C5-fluoroketone (C5-FK) have emerged as some of the (more/most) potential options due to their low environmental impact. This article reports on the breakdown performance of these gases/gas mixtures under 50 Hz AC and 1.2/50 μs lightning impulse (LI) voltages at 1.3 bar absolute pressure in a 10 mm rod-plane gap with a weakly nonuniform field relevant to medium voltage applications. In general, the mixture of technical air with C5-FK was found to exhibit superior dielectric performance to CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> or technical air when stressed with both AC and LI voltages. For all the studied gases/gas mixtures, the breakdown voltage and its scatter were found to be higher under negative LI stress, indicating a lack of initial electrons. The results are also compared to those of SF6 and a mixture of 13.6% C5-FK in air, which were tested during the round-robin test campaign by the CIGRE D1.67 working group using similar methods and test configurations. Findings from this study will therefore aid in the development of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>-free switchgears as comparison of the results would provide the data required for design optimization.

articleTitle: The Eroding DBA Detection in AC Inclined Plane Tracking and Erosion Test Using UHF Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In this work, ultra-high frequency detection of eroding dry band arcing is employed as an online and non-intrusive technique to identify deep erosion failure during the AC inclined plane test. To this end, tests are conducted on silicone rubber under three different voltages, while simultaneously measuring leakage current, surface temperature, and ultra-high frequency signals using a horn antenna. No ultra-high frequency detection is obtained during the mild dry band arcing in the test, which does not lead to erosion. In contrast, detection becomes evident during stable dry-band arcing activity, particularly when the intensity becomes significant. Ultra-high frequency measurements indicate that the intensity of detection increases with the severity of eroding dry-band arcing during the test and with higher test voltages.

articleTitle: Experimental and Theoretical Research on Enhanced Visible Light Photocatalytic Performance of N-Doped TiO2 Dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In this paper, in order to improve the response of functional dielectric TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to visible light, doping modification method was adopted to realize the degradation of organic pollutants under natural light. The sol-gel method was used to prepare pure TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and N-doped TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticle with doping ratio of 5at%, 10at% and 20at%. Photocatalytic properties of the samples were evaluated under UV and visible light respectively. The results show that N successfully enters the crystal lattice of anatase TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and the N-doping modification significantly improves the absorption ability of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> at visible wavelengths. The 10at% doped samples showed the best photocatalytic degradation efficiency under two kinds of light conditions. The results of density functional calculation of two N doping structures (substitution-doping and gap-doping) show that N doping introduces impurity levels from the hybridization of N 2p into the band gap of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,</inf> reduces the effective band gap width, and causes the absorption edge to redshift, which gives a reasonable explanation for the experimental phenomenon.

articleTitle: Investigation of Dielectric and Thermal Properties of iPP/MA-PP/TPU Blends
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Isotactic polypropylene (iPP)-based blends have been widely investigated for their potential as next-generation insulating materials for high voltage cables. Pure iPP is too brittle; hence, blends with various elastomers have been developed. In the present work, maleic anhydride grafted polypropylene (MA-PP) is used as a compatibilizer, enhancing its compatibility with thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) elastomer in an attempt to prepare and characterize iPP/MA-PP/TPU blends. This study investigates the thermal properties, molecular structure, and dielectric performance of these blends using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), Fourier-Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and dielectric spectroscopy (DS). The results reveal that the introduction of maleic anhydride (MA) into the blends results in the formation of imide structures, through crosslinking with the TPU, that do not affect the crystallinity and melting point of iPP. The iPP/MA-PP/TPU blends display increased dielectric permittivity and losses in the low frequency domain; characteristics that are dependent on the concentration of MA.

articleTitle: An Optical Measurement Method for Electrostatic Sensing Based on Fabry-Perot Interference Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Optical electrostatic sensors play an essential function in the development of digitalization and intelligence of power systems due to their passive, anti-electromagnetic interference, and fast response speeds. However, the performance of optical electrostatic sensors is affected by the collector size. In this paper, the dynamic output characteristics of fiber optic electrostatic sensors with different collector sizes are tested. Meanwhile, models of different sizes of collectors are also constructed and simulated and analyzed. The results show that the sensitivity of the sensor increases with the increase of the collector area. The sensitivity of the sensor with a 5 cm radius collector is 53.1 pm/kV. This study provides meaningful insights for the design and optimization of electrostatic sensors.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on the Corona Inception Field of HVDC Conductor Under Different Air Pressure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: When HVDC transmission lines pass through high-altitude areas, the impact of low pressure will cause a change in the corona inception field of the wires. Through simulation experiments, The influence of air pressure on the corona inception field of DC conductor can be obtained, providing data support for the electromagnetic environment prediction of HVDC transmission lines in high-altitude areas. In this paper, A wire-plate electrode experimental platform is established in the artificial climate chamber with controllable temperature, humidity and pressure. An experiment on the influence of air pressure on the corona inception field of DC conductor is carried out by using the wire with diameters of 3mm and 5mm, The experiment involved measuring the ground electric field under positive and negative polarity wires at altitudes ranging from 0 to 4000m. The corona onset voltage of the wire is determined using a fitting method based on the ground electric field data under different pressures, and the corona inception field of the wires is calculated accordingly. The experimental results show that with the increase of altitude (the decrease of air pressure), the corona inception field of the same diameter wire approximately presents a linear decline trend. The linear function can be used to reflect the relationship between the corona inception field and the change of air pressure. The larger the radius of the conductor, the smaller the absolute value of the slope <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> in the linear fitting function, the corona inception field on the surface of the conductor decreases at a slower rate with increasing altitude. In other words, for every 1000m increase in altitude, there is a smaller decrease in corona inception field.

articleTitle: Dielectric Testing of Gas Mixtures with Air, Volatile Organic Compounds and Carbon Oxides
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The present work summarizes the results obtained while testing a rod-to-plane gap with switching-like voltage impulses different in gas mixtures. Gas mixtures including technical air, carbon monoxide and dioxide, benzene, toluene, and ethanol were tested. A sealed chamber was used for the high voltage testing of a rod-to-plane gap with switching-like voltage impulses. For all gas mixtures tested, an increment of the 50% breakdown voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{U_{50\%}})$</tex> with respect to the reference gas (technical air) was measured, up to 38% for the gas mixture with carbon oxides. A higher <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{U_{50\%}}$</tex> with respect to the technical air was measured for all tested gas mixtures, for both polarities. The estimated streamer inception voltage for the gas mixtures containing carbon oxides was below the measured breakdown voltages.

articleTitle: Measurements of Space Charge Distributions in PMMA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Spontaneous dielectric failure can be precipitated by space charge accumulation when dielectric materials are exposed to charged particle irradiation. Events of this nature are believed to occur in satellite dielectrics. This has prompted a need for a method of measuring charge accumulation in bulk dielectric samples when exposed to charged particle irradiation, even in the presence of surface ion neutralization. A Pulsed Electro Acoustic (PEA) system has been constructed to this end. 2.5 cm thick, polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA) sheets were charged by a 6 MeV nominal electron beam and interrogated by the PEA system. These experimental results were also compared to Monte Carlo radiation transport results with imposed internal electric fields due to the space charge.

articleTitle: Interface Charge Characteristics of XLPE-EPDM Double Layers with Different Silicone Grease Coated
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Space charge measurements were conducted on double-layer dielectric materials of XLPE and EPDM with common-used silicone grease (CSG) and fluorosilicone grease (FSG) coated at the interface. The conductivities and dielectric constants of the four materials were also tested. The study found that the interfacial charges increase with the applied electric field for both coated XLPE/EPDM samples. Bipolar charges appear at both coated XLPE/EPDM interfaces under low electric field strength, with a polarity opposite to the adjacent dielectric. These bipolar charges gradually disappear as the field strength increases. When the interface is coated with common-used silicone grease, the polarity transition of the interfacial charge at the XLPE/EPDM interface aligns with the Maxwell-Wagner-Sillars polarization model. However, this alignment does not occur when the interface is coated with FSG. With the application of FSG, there is a significant increase in the accumulation of negative charges at the interface, and the rate of interfacial charge establishment and dissipation at the beginning of the voltage on and off is faster compared to the interface coated with CSG.

articleTitle: Pasteurization of Escherichia Coli in ICE using Voltage Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper reports the pasteurization of Escherichia coli in frozen NaCl solutions by applying freezing and voltage. The experimental samples consisted of frozen NaCl solutions containing E. coli. We applied DC or AC voltage to the frozen samples stored in freezers at -20°C or -60°C. The results were as follows: In the -20°C freezer, the bactericidal effect on E. coli in frozen 0.01 and 0.53 mol/L NaCl solutions with DC voltage application was higher than with freezing alone (no voltage application). Conversely, AC voltage application to the frozen NaCl solutions showed no bactericidal effect. At -60°C, applying DC 500 V to the frozen NaCl solutions showed no bactericidal effect. Additionally, glycerin in the frozen NaCl solutions inhibited the pasteurization effect of freezing and voltage application. However, adding ethanol to the frozen 0.53 mol/L NaCl solutions enhanced the bactericidal effect of freezing and voltage application.

articleTitle: Measurement of Streamer Radii in SF6 Alternatives: Mixtures of CO2/O2 and C4F7N in CO2/O2
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Streamer discharges are imaged in three gas mixtures of interest for high voltage insulation equipment - 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>02/90% CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, 30% O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/ 70% CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and 5% C4-FN / 50% O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/ 90% CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The radii of streamer channels are evaluated, and the scaling constant for the inverse law relationship between the streamer radius and pressure is determined. In CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> /O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> mixtures, a scaling constant of 12 - 20 Pa m for positive streamers and 20 - 35 Pa <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> for negative streamers is found. In the C4-FN/ CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> /O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> mixture, a value of 13 - 18 Pa m for positive streamers and 18 - 25 Pa <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> for negative streamers fits the evaluated radii. The scaling constant is a crucial parameter when modelling the breakdown process in these mixtures and the radii values can be utilized for validating numerical streamer simulation codes.

articleTitle: Corona Inception and Breakdown in High-Altitude, Low-Pressure Air under Negative DC Voltage for Aircraft Electrification Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The achievement of the net-zero emission goal is considered contingent upon the implementation of transportation electrification. Presently, all-electric commercial vehicles are restricted to land and water transport. The prospect of complete electrification of aircraft, particularly the plausible realization of all-electric aircraft (AEA), is acknowledged as being imminent. Within the electric power system (EPS) designs proposed for AEA, medium DC voltage systems in the order of up to a few tens of kilovolts are employed. Challenges manifest in the management of such voltages within a low-pressure environment. One of the emerging challenges pertains to the partial discharge (PD) behavior under DC stress, a phenomenon acknowledged to exhibit pressure- and field-dependent variations.
