The importance of studying the dynamics of pre-breakdown and breakdown phenomena in such environments is underscored by the fact that air serves as a crucial insulator for the EPS in AEA. Accordingly, this experimental study aims to comprehend the behavior of air subjected to high negative DC voltages and offer insights into the PD onset dynamics, specifically corona inception and breakdown. This investigation utilizes a needle-to-plane electrode configuration, examining its performance under a standard range of aviation-specific pressures across varying air gaps. The findings of this study contribute to the development of reliable electrical insulation systems tailored to withstand the demanding conditions encountered during aircraft operation.

articleTitle: Impact of High-Frequency Repetitive Bipolar Square Wave Voltages on the Lifetime of Turn-to-Turn Insulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Emerging power electronic drives and converters are planned to operate at high voltages with high switching frequencies (up to a few hundred kHz), which will affect the reliability of insulation systems of windings of electrical machines. To evaluate the insulation quality under such high-frequency pulses, lifetime test is a prominent way. For simplification of test procedure, turn-to-turn insulation samples are approved by IEC 60034-18-42. In past studies, the impact of switching frequencies has been investigated under lower frequencies (up to 20 kHz), which cannot address the challenges of next-generation wide bandgap (WBG)-based power converters. In this study, the lifetimes of turn-to-turn insulations under high switching frequencies (50 kHz) are tested at four different rise times (50 ns, 100 ns, 150 ns, 200 ns), and the impact of switching frequency on the lifetime of the insulation is analyzed.

articleTitle: Effect of Interphase Dielectric Property in Electric Field Distribution in Silicone Elastomer Nanocomposite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The emergence of ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) devices results in increasing research in high-density and high-temperature power electronic (PE) packaging. Encapsulants are crucial for electronic packaging and are required to be functional at high-density, high temperatures in UWBG-based power electronic devices. Silicone (Si)-based gels and elastomers, popularly used as encapsulations in conventional power electronic packaging, show dielectric issues under high-density and high-temperature systems. The local electric field enhancement at triple points in the high-power density PE devices increases the risk of partial discharge (PD). Adding nano-fillers in Si-based elastomers is one of the approaches to increase the dielectric integrity of high-power density devices. The high-volume fraction of interphase between the nanoparticles and polymers improves the dielectric properties. The interphase power model relates the dielectric constant of polymer composites with the dielectric constant of the interphase layer. In this paper, a numerical study has been conducted to investigate the effect of interphase dielectric constant on the electric field mitigation at the triple points Si-elastomer-based nanocomposites. A numerical model is developed in COMSOL Multiphysics to investigate the effect of interphase dielectric property on electric field distribution in the encapsulant of PE modules. Furthermore, the effect of nano-filler dielectric properties in minimizing the local electric field is compared.

articleTitle: Modeling Permittivity Measurements of Thin Film Materials Versus Film Thickness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Measured permittivity values of thin film polymeric samples were substantially less for thin samples, but asymptotically approached bulk values above <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 500\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 25 \mu \mathbf{m}$</tex> samples the observed permittivity values were as much as 50% less than for bulk measurements. This behavior has been studied for four common homogeneous polymeric materials for sample thickness in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 3000\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. To quantify these observations, an empirical single-parameter model was developed to correct measured permittivity of thin samples based on an effective stray capacitance in series with the samples to compensate for effects attributed to instrumentation.

articleTitle: Effect of Dehydration Using Glycerin on Electrical Properties of Vegetable-Based-Oil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper reports on the impact of dehydration using glycerin on the electrical properties of vegetable-based oil after an esterification reaction. The experimental sample oil, containing a specific amount of distilled water, was treated with reagent glycerin and glycerin extracted from the esterification reaction. The findings indicate that (i) AC dielectric breakdown strength (Fb) and volume resistivity were enhanced by the elimination of moisture in the vegetable-based oil ester, (ii) viscosity remained unaffected by moisture content, (iii) the combined use of reagent glycerin and extracted glycerin effectively removed moisture from the vegetable-based oil, and (iv) reagent glycerin exhibited superior effectiveness in both moisture removal and improvement of electrical properties compared to extracted glycerin.

articleTitle: Monitoring Oxidation in Natural Ester Insulating Liquids Through FTIR Spectroscopy Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This study investigates the thermal aging behavior of MIDEL eN1204, a natural ester-based insulating oil derived from rapeseed, using Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy as the primary analytical method. The oil samples were subjected to an intensive thermal aging process at 115°C for 1000 hours to replicate the long-term aging process that occurs in transformers. FTIR spectroscopy was employed to monitor shifts in key absorbance bands indicative of oxidative and hydrolytic degradation. The 1711 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> band, associated with carbonyl compounds, showed a significant increase in intensity, marking the oil's degradation. A differential normalization approach was introduced to enhance the detection of these aging effects. The results demonstrate the potential of FTIR spectroscopy to improve diagnostic processes of natural ester insulating liquids for maintaining transformer insulation systems.

articleTitle: Developing an MVDC Bipolar Coaxial Cable System for Lunar Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The increasing need for power on the lunar surface, expected to reach megawatt levels, aligns with NASA's goal of establishing a sustainable human presence on the Moon, able to support over 100 personnel indefinitely. As humanity explores sustained lunar habitation and aims to establish bases, efficient and reliable power transmission becomes crucial. Power lines with high power density are needed, focusing on weight and volume while ensuring safety and cost-effectiveness in the harsh lunar environment. There are three possible locations for power lines on the lunar surface: above, on, or below the surface. Due to harsh lunar conditions like temperature fluctuations, micro meteoroid impacts, and radiation exposure, the initial two methods have limited effectiveness in transferring power on the moon. Underground deployment is considered safe and convenient; however, low soil thermal conductivity could pose a challenge. However, a temperature of -23.15 °C at a depth of 30 cm proves beneficial for waste heat. This study employs COMSOL Multiphysics to propose a novel method for developing and analyzing bipolar MVDC cables for power transmission beneath the lunar surface. Designed for ±10 kV voltage and 2 MW power, these cables offer an efficient solution for lunar power transmission and are resilient to harsh conditions.

articleTitle: Phenomena of AC and DC Breakdown in Oxidized Polypropylene
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: To estimate the insulation performance of polypropylene (PP) material through its lifetime for cable application, thin PP films (~100 μm thick) were aged at the temperature of 150°C in a fan-assisted oven for up to 21 days. With the chosen ageing conditions, the polymer chains were attacked by heat energy and reacted with available oxygen, forming chemical products in undersurface region from the initial stage, notably carbonyl groups, whose concentration increases along with the ageing periods, as detected by the Fourier-Transform Infrared (FTIR) Spectroscopy in the present work. The breakdown performance was examined by applying ramp voltage at a rate of 500 V/s under AC and DC stress, respectively. It has been observed that after ageing, the AC breakdown strength (BDS) declines from 211.01 ± 2.71 to 197.43 ± 3.02 kV/mm, while the DC BDS initially increases from 506.15 ± 18.27 to 550.94 ± 19.39 kV/mm at 14 days of ageing, followed by a decrease with any further ageing. The observed difference is attributed to the different breakdown regions: AC breakdown is more likely to occur adjacent to the sample surface. The continuous decline versus ageing durations correlates with the higher concentration of carbonyl groups detected on the sample surface. On the other hand, DC breakdown tends to occur within the bulk of sample. The changes in BDS after ageing is related to the electric field distortion due to the space charge distribution induced by the chemical alterations.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Current Distribution in 2D Polycrystalline Material Using Monte Carlo Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Polycrystalline materials consist of crystalline grains whose electrical properties may vary due to grain size, orientation, and intragranular boundaries, causing non-uniform current distribution. This study employs Monte Carlo Method to simulate current distribution trend in polycrystalline materials, utilizing its ability of analyzing system with a high degree of complexity and randomness. A simplified 2D resistive network is used to model grains within polycrystalline material, and Kirchhoff's Current Law is used to solve mesh-loop currents. The simulations highlight the variability in current distribution caused by inhomogeneity of grain properties. The results revealed that contact interface inhomogeneity significantly impacts internal current distribution statistics, and that improved bulk phase homogeneity increases susceptibility to concentrated current distribution caused by contact/interface inhomogeneity. These findings emphasize the need to consider material quality of both bulk phase and contact layer when optimizing the electrical performance of polycrystalline materials.

articleTitle: Improving Surface Flashover Voltages of Alumina Insulators by Applying Titanium Dioxide Coatings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Experimental results of the improvement in the surface flashover voltage of an alumina insulator in vacuum achieved by applying a TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> coating are reported. We used a needle with a sharp tip made of conductive diamond as a cathode to easily repeat the measurements. In each measurement run, the applied voltage was ramped up until discharge occurred. The obtained average surface-flashover voltages of alumina with and without TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> coating are −7.4 kV and −24.9 kV, respectively. This improvement is attributed to a lower secondary electron emission yield and a reduced electric field at the cathode triple junction, and a lower degree of surface charging.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Modelling of the Dielectric Response of the Components of a Composite Insulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The dielectric composite found in the ISIS dipole bending magnets has been investigated using broadband dielectric spectroscopy. Frequency scans obtained at different temperatures have been plotted. Master curves have been constructed above the glass transition temperature in order to obtain activation energies via Arrhenius plots. Dielectric relaxation and charge transport mechanisms have been observed in the frequency spectra with different activation energies. A generic equivalent circuit model (ECM) has been constructed from the dielectric data and validated for all components of the composite dielectric.

articleTitle: Effects of Temperature on the Partial Discharge Characteristics of Silicone Oil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: High voltage cable systems tend to have a higher risk of insulation failure at joints and terminations than the main body. One of the insulating liquids used in cable sealing end (CSE) is silicone oil. Increase in temperature is known to affect the physical and dielectric properties of insulation materials. This study investigates the partial discharge characteristics of a silicone oil at different temperatures from 20 °C to 80 °C. The sample used in this study is a high-viscosity silicone oil, which has a dynamic viscosity of 13,000 cP at 20 °C. From the PD measurements obtained, it showed that partial discharge inception voltages (PDIV) are comparable at different temperatures. The PD magnitude showed consistent results at various temperatures indicating insignificant effect of temperature on the PD magnitude. On the other hand, PD repetition rate decreased with the increase of temperature where the PD repetition rate at 80 °C is 30% lower than that at 20 °C at applied voltage of 45 kV.

articleTitle: HVDC Defect Identification: Partial Discharges Signal Acquisition and Machine Learning Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The aim of this work is to achieve effective features to enable machine learning algorithms to identify defects and incipient faults in the case of insulating systems used for high-voltage direct current (HVDC) applications. Partial discharge (PD) testing and analysis has become a key tool in all aspects of the design, commissioning, maintenance and monitoring of AC and DC insulating systems. In this study, PD measurements were conducted on a medium voltage (MV) cable segment with artificial defects. These measurements were performed under a negative HVDC power supply using various sensors, including a High Frequency Current Transformer (HFCT), a Rogowski Coil, and a VHF Antenna. The acquired signals were post-processed using the Normalized Auto-correlation Function (NACF). The 3D NACF space plots have been obtained by selecting the three larger dispersion components obtained by the comparison of the NACF of the acquired signals. The objective was to analyze the differences in the measured PD signal data obtained with the three different sensors using machine learning algorithms. This analysis provides insights into the effectiveness of the developed features and their potential when different kind of sensors are used for the detection of faults in case of HVDC applications.

articleTitle: Effect of Voltage and Insulation Layer Thickness on the Temperature Rise Process of Polyester Film-Wrapped Coil in Instrument Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The overheating phenomenon of instrument transformers may threaten their safe and stable operation in power grid. Through finite element (FEM) simulation, the temperature rising process of instrument transformers can be predicted, providing scientific basis for optimizing design and improving work reliability. A two-dimensional axisymmetric polyester film wrapped coil geometric model was established, and the electromagnetic and solid heat transfer equations were used in the Electrothermal coupling computation. The effect of voltage variation (500V-2000V) of coil on instrument transformer heating was investigated. Under normal conditions, the Temperature of the coil increased approximately linearly in the first 2 days and reached their highest values, then became stable. The maximum temperature of a coil with a voltage of 2000V was 108.5K higher than that of a coil with a voltage of 500V. The Electrothermal coupling model could well predicate the temperature raising process of coils in instrument transformers under different voltages. The higher voltage significantly increases the highest temperature of the coil under different operation conditions. The highest temperature of the instrument transformer was at the terminal of the coil.

articleTitle: Interaction Between Electric Field Profile and Partial Discharges Simultaneously Detected in a Loaded HVDC Cable: PDs Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This study aims to examine the relationship between electric field distribution and the initiation of partial discharge (PD). The test subject is a DC model cable with an air void defect, exposed to both electrical stress and a thermal gradient. Electric field distributions were determined based on space charge measurements using an innovative Pulsed Electroacoustic (PEA) cell, while PD activity was tracked using a PryCam sensor. By acquiring data on space charge and PD phenomena simultaneously, the interaction between these phenomena is clarified. The results indicate that the electric field distribution along the cable's radial direction changes over time. Initially, the electric field has a Laplacian distribution, but this inverts after 20 minutes of voltage application. This inversion increases the electric field at the cable's outer radius, where the air void defect is located, causing the partial discharge inception electric field within the defect to reach 17.8 kV/mm in the unaffected section of the cable. This paper represents the second part of a single work. In the first part, the PEA measurement aspect is described in detail. In this second part, the analysis of the PDs, their separation by means of a clustering algorithm and comparison with the electric field distributions obtained are examined in detail.

articleTitle: Interaction Between Electric Field Profile and Partial Discharges Simultaneously Detected in a Loaded HVDC Cable: Space Charge Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The aim of this work is to evaluate the correlation between electric field distribution and the onset of partial discharge. The specimen under test is a DC model cable containing an air void defect and subjected to both electrical stress and thermal gradient. The electric field distributions have been calculated starting from the space charge detected by means of a novel PEA cell. While, the partial discharge activity has been monitored by means of the PryCam sensor. The space charge and partial discharge phenomena have been simultaneously acquired in order to make clearer the interaction between both phenomena. Measurement results show that the electric field distribution along the radial direction of the cable is variable over time. The initial Laplacian distribution of the field results inverted after 20 minutes of voltage application. After this time interval, the electric field in the external cable radius, where the air void defect is located, is increased. Therefore, the partial discharge inception electric field within the defect results reached and equal to 17.8 kV/mm in the healthy cable section. This paper represents the first part of this investigation and it is focused on the description of the novel PEA cell, on the explanation of the measurement setup and on the evaluation of the obtained charges and electric field distributions. The second part of this study, instead, is focused on the analysis and description of the observed partial discharge activity.

articleTitle: Influence of Degassing Process on AC Breakdown Behavior of XLPE Insulation in Power Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The degassing process during the production of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) insulated cables leads to non-uniform changes in both the content of by-products and the aggregated structure within the insulation, significantly affecting the breakdown behavior of the insulation layers. This paper investigates the AC breakdown characteristics of the inner, middle, and outer layers of XLPE cable insulation at different degassing durations, with a focus on the impact of by-product content and crystalline morphology on the breakdown mechanism. The results show that degassing effectively reduces the number of polar small molecular by-products within the insulation and promotes further perfection of the crystalline structure, reducing the proportion of amorphous regions, and improving the internal electric field distortion of the insulation, thereby enhancing the breakdown field strength. This phenomenon is more pronounced in the outer layer of the insulation.

articleTitle: Electrical Analyses of Gamma Radiation-Induced Aging on EPDM-Based Insulation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper deals with the investigation of the insulating properties of EPDM materials subjected to radiation aging with two non-destructive techniques: electrical (dielectric spectroscopy) and chemical (FTIR). Flat samples of EPDM were subjected to accelerated aging at 860 Gy/h for 664 h with four withdrawals at room temperature. The dielectric spectroscopy results indicate that the tan δ at 100 kHz coherently follows the aging evolution of the materials and it is suggested to be a suitable aging marker. The spectra of FTIR results suggest that EPDM undergoes chain scission and oxidation after radiation ageing. These results confirm the suitability of the electrical nondestructive technique for aging evaluation.

articleTitle: Dielectric Analysis on Aqueous Solutions by a High-Precision Double-Logarithmic-Derivative Method for Relaxation Frequency Calculation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In this paper, cooling dielectric spectra of NaCl and KCl aqueous solutions with different concentrations from 10°C to -60°C were first measured and the corresponding crystallization and dielectric relaxation behavior were analyzed. Subsequently, by establishing a high-precision double-logarithmic-derivative method, dielectric relaxation frequencies contained in dielectric spectra were accurately calculated. Furthermore, with the help of this proposed method, the relaxation polarization time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\tau}$</tex> and the activation energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{E}_{\mathbf{a}}$</tex> of water molecules in composite ice formed by low-temperature aqueous solutions with different concentrations were calculated and analyzed. The results indicate that the accuracy of relaxation frequency identification reaches 2.10-4.67 times that of classical methods. As the concentration ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\beta}$</tex> increases, the relaxation time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\tau}$</tex> of water molecules in composite ice formed by low-temperature solution rapidly decreases and the activation energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{E}_{\mathbf{a}}$</tex> significantly increases when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{0} < \boldsymbol{\beta}\leq \boldsymbol{0.5}$</tex>. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\beta}\geq \boldsymbol{1}, \boldsymbol{\tau}$</tex> slowly increases and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{E}_{\mathbf{a}}$</tex> gradually decreases. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{E}_{\mathbf{a}}-\boldsymbol{\beta}$</tex> curves of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{NaCl}$</tex> composite ice and KCl composite ice show maximum values at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\beta}_{\mathbf{NaCl}}=\boldsymbol{0.56}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta_{\text{KCl}}=0.62$</tex>, respectively.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis between Measured and Simulated Pulse Voltage Distribution in Form Wound Stator Winding of Inverter-Fed Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation study of a pulse voltage distribution within the windings of a motor using a high-frequency (HF) equivalent circuit model. The simulation results are validated by comparison with measured data, aimed at enhancing insulation design technology for next-generation inverter-fed motors. The investigation focuses on pulse voltage propagation between each coil-to-ground and turn-to-turn in the initial winding, which is crucial for selecting the optimal insulation design for evaluation. The subject of this study is an inverter-fed three-phase induction motor with a rated output of 75 kW and a rated voltage of 3kV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</inf>. The winding configuration consists of two parallel wound types with 10 turns and 16 windings per phase, featuring 4 poles. The impulse voltage used had a rise time of 250 ns, a pulse width of 50μs, and a voltage amplitude of 1000 V. An impulse voltage was applied from the beginning to the end of Phase U, and output waveforms at each measurement point were obtained. Additionally, the output voltage waveforms for each turn were simulated using the developed HF equivalent circuit model, implemented in LTspice® (Analog Devices), a transient phenomenon simulation software, and compared with the measured results. The simulated results show good agreement with the measured results. The maximum simulated voltages matched measured values within an error margin of less than 3.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> for coil-to-ground and 9.5% for turn-to-turn in the initial winding. The developed HF equivalent circuit model is validated as a useful tool for evaluating surge voltage impacts in the insulation design of stator windings.

articleTitle: Multi-Frequency Impedance Characteristic of Long-Time Operating DC-Link Capacitor in HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The DC-link capacitor is one of the most vulnerable components of the modular multilevel converter (MMC) in an operating HVDC system. To assess the aging states of DC-link capacitors, the characteristics of capacitor impedance in a multi-frequency range are investigated and analyzed. First, the equivalent circuit model is established with consideration of the insulation resistance of the DC-link capacitor. Then, the multi-frequency impedance spectra of capacitors under five aging states are detected by a high-precision measuring bridge. The experimental result shows that as the aging degree of the capacitor increases, the inflection point of the capacitance spectrum in a multi-frequency range tends to move to a higher frequency. Meanwhile, the spectrum of the resistance in a multi-frequency range shows a growing slope at low frequency range (< 200 Hz), and the resistance value approaches a stable level at high frequency range. Further, the above findings can be verified based on the equivalent circuit method mentioned above. The multi-frequency characteristics of capacitors can not only evaluate the aging degree of the deteriorated capacitors, but also be utilized to identify deterioration causes including the capacitance loss, the conductive path resistance increase, the dielectric insulation deterioration, etc. The proposed method can provide a novel perspective on detection of DC-link capacitor aging.

articleTitle: Flexible All-organic Composites with Ultrahigh Energy Storage Density for Wearable Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In In this study, we present a novel approach to fabricating flexible energy storage ultracapacitors. While dielectric polymers have traditionally been employed in the production of energy storage capacitors, significant efforts over the past two decades have focused on improving their energy storage capabilities through the use of composite materials, primarily inorganic-polymer composites. In contrast, our work explores the use of all-organic composites, combining polymers with organic small molecules. These all-organic composites not only offer superior flexibility compared to conventional dielectric polymers, but they also exhibit enhanced energy storage performance. For example, the energy storage density of composites made from P(VDF-CTFE) or P(VDF-HFP) mixed with silane exceeds that of the pure polymer counterparts. These improvements make all-organic composites promising candidates for the development of flexible energy storage devices, particularly for applications in wearable electronics.

articleTitle: Effect of Electric Field on Conductivity of Palm Fatty Acid Ester
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Biodegradable ester oils have emerged as an environmentally sustainable alternative to traditional mineral oils in various applications. New uses, particularly in converter transformers, energy storage systems, and HVDC transformers, are under continuous investigation. The electrical conductivity of insulating materials is a key parameter for these novel applications; however, limited research has been conducted on the conductivity of biodegradable ester oils in comparison to mineral oil. This study examines the influence of electric field strength on the conductivity σ of palm fatty acid esters (PFAE) under DC voltage application ranging from 10 to 3000 seconds, and compares the results with those of mineral oil. The experimental results indicated that σ of PFAE decreases over time under electric fields ranging from 100 V/mm to 1 kV/mm, but increases with time under fields exceeding 1 kV/mm. Notably, the conductivity in long-term measurements was lower than in short-term measurements. When comparing the conductivities of PFAE, mineral oil, and synthetic esters, PFAE exhibited the highest conductivity across both short- and long-term measurements and various electric field strengths. This difference is attributed to the lower kinematic viscosity of PFAE compared to mineral oils and synthetic esters. The significant effect of kinematic viscosity on the conductivity was observed among the ester oils, with the ratio of conductivities closely matching the ratio of their kinematic viscosities. Furthermore, a comparison between ester oil and mineral oil revealed a more than 100-fold difference in conductivity, primarily due to the effect of ionic carrier conduction in the presence or absence of polar groups. Additionally, the higher charge density in ester-based insulating oils compared to mineral oils was identified as a contributing factor to this disparity.

articleTitle: Analyzing DC Partial Discharge Characteristics of Voids Defect in MVDC Switchboard Cable Terminations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In DC power equipment, the switchboard is connected via a termination when the cable is connected from the outside. In the termination, multilayer interfaces are formed between XLPE and semi-conductive layer. Void defects occur between the multilayer interfaces due to various causes during cable connection, which causes damage due to partial discharge inside the termination. Therefore, this paper simulates the multilayer interface of XLPE-semi-conductive layer of switchboard cable termination to fabricated partial discharge simulation defect electrodes, and experiments were conducted under three different conditions by varying the size of the voids. The experiments were conducted at a temperature of 70 ° C to account for the rising temperature conditions at termination during operation. The discharge magnitude increases proportionally with both applied voltage and void size. In addition, discharges are larger and more frequently proportional to the applied voltage and void size. The characteristics of void partial discharges show that over time, the occurrence frequency increases, ceases at a certain point, and then increases again.

articleTitle: Dielectric Biosensor for E. Coli Detection with DC Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This study presents a novel approach for detecting E. coli using dielectric properties enhanced by DC bias. Traditional methods for detecting bacteria often require extensive sample preparation and are hindered by the composition of the solutes in complex liquid backgrounds, and this proposed method overcomes these challenges by utilizing dielectric measurement with DC bias. Aluminum rod electrodes and planar stainless-steel electrodes connected to an impedance analyzer were used to measure the capacitance of liquid samples containing E. coli across a frequency spectrum from 40 Hz to 100 M Hz. Results indicated that the presence of E. coli significantly reduced the change in capacitance when DC bias was applied and removed, suggesting that DC bias is an effective stimulus for E. coli detection in various liquids. Further analysis indicated that the effects were predominantly from the electric double-layer region. This technique effectively leverages the intrinsic properties of bacterial liquid and their response to specific stimuli, which may improve the robustness and accuracy of bacteria detection in complex environments.

articleTitle: Ageing, Space Charge and Lifetime of Polymeric Insulating Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In the present paper, an attempt has been made to explore trap parameters as an ageing marker to assess polymeric insulating material status. The approach has been established on the principle that ageing is the result of changes of materials, including both chemical and physical changes. In terms of energy band theory, these changes will alter energy structures, resulting in extra energy levels in the forbidden gap, i.e. traps. By measuring charge dynamics in the aged material, it is possible to extract charge trap parameters. Using these changes in trap parameter, the status of the material can be revealed. To simplify the approach, two-level energy traps have been introduced in the present paper.

articleTitle: Humidity Dependent Charge Formation in Air under DC field Below Partial Discharge Inception
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This study investigates the influence of humidity, electric field strength, and electrode geometry on charge formation and accumulation dynamics at electrode-air-polymer interfaces under DC conditions below the partial discharge inception level. Utilizing a structured test matrix with varying voltages and electrode radii, experiments were conducted in a controlled environment where humidity levels ranged from 40% to 90%. The results reveal that lower voltage levels and larger electrode radii significantly heighten sensitivity to humidity changes, affecting charge accumulation patterns at the dielectric-air interface. Notably, high humidity conditions (~98% RH) demonstrated that water condensation on electrodes can inhibit charge generation. Surface potential measurements with a Kelvin probe is utilized to quantify these effects, highlighting the complex interaction among air humidity, electric field strength, and time in influencing charge formation. This study enhances the understanding of charge dynamics critical for improving the reliability and performance of HVDC insulation systems.

articleTitle: Calculation of Television Interference (TVI) for Unconventional High Surge Impedance Loading (HSIL) Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Television Interference (TVI) is a pivotal factor in high voltage transmission line design. TVI occurs because of corona discharges along the transmission line, causing signal deterioration and power loss. Conventional lines have the bundled conductors symmetrically placed on a circle, and the bundle radius is chosen such that the corona discharge effects are reduced. High Surge Impedance Loading (HSIL) transmission lines consist of a higher number of subconductors and a larger bundle radius, increasing line loadability. Conductor costs are reduced by using subconductors with smaller radii. The novel 500 kV unconventional HSIL line designed in this paper exhibits a potential to enhance the natural power of the line and differ from the conventional HSIL and the conventional lines in having asymmetrical bundled conductor configurations. For this unconventional HSIL line, TVI produced due to corona discharges on and around the line are calculated and compared to the conventional line. As a result of this study, we are taking a step forward toward the development of unconventional HSIL lines for modern power systems that will revolutionize power delivery.

articleTitle: Photon and UHF PD Property of Wire Metal Particles in SF6
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Wire Metal particle is a typical defect with serious harm in Gas insulated switchgear (GIS). In this paper, phase-resolved photon signals of an adhered aluminum wire at AC are measured using a model basin insulation spacer. PD signals are also measured simultaneously using a UHF PD sensor. The findings reveal that photon counting is capable of detecting the optical signals preceding PD caused by metal particles, and the PRPCbased features effectively illuminate the characteristics of photon responses elicited by such defects. Collectively, this research introduces a potential approach to the detection of wire metal particles in GIS.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge and Electrical Treeing Behavior of High-Voltage Power Module - A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Packaging materials and structures partial discharge (PD) and electrical treeing behavior, emanating from the encapsulant-ceramic-metallization interface called the triple point, poses a significant challenge in the reliability of high-voltage (HV) power modules. It is crucial to provide an overview of the current understanding of PD and electrical treeing behavior in HV power modules. This paper will summarize PD behavior under square-wave voltage and the understanding of the electrical treeing phenomenon. In addition, critical research topics related to PD and electrical treeing degradation that need further investigation will be identified.
